I discovered this banana at a street market in South America. I did a double take. The skin of this banana is RED , the inside is a very intense yellow.

This banana can be enjoyed without cooking but is excellent when fried or used to make desserts. One bite of a ripe one and I was hooked!

be warned

Although it does not produce as much as commercial banana plants, once you taste it, you want to have more!

I grew this plant for many years and was my pride and joy :)

Like all bananas it likes rich soil and lots of mulch and water. The soil must also drain very quickly, it does not like to be in a puddle.

An advantage to this banana is its resistance to pests and diseases.

The original use of this banana was to make beer, spirits, wine and vinegar which have medicinal properties. The vinegar itself is a true delicacy and a fine wine can be made with it. The sugar content is such that it lends itself well to fermentation.

It was the original banana to be imported in Canada! But it fell out of favor because of big agro.

They will give their first cache of bananas after 2 years and start producing suckers one year in.

Once the bananas starts appearing it is good to keep them in a cloth bag at night to prevent bats from eating the shit out of them.

For rodents, bull nettle and thorny plants are your ally. Plant them at the base or just keep a patch in your garden reserved for these plants and chop them down when you see the bananas start to form. Place them at the base and make sure other trees are not touching the canopy, I have seen rats leap from tree to tree like monkeys!

Once you have harvested the bananas, do not chop down the mother plant, the suckers will suck it dry and be healthier.

If you want to take a cutting, you need to have your hose and a chisel (sharp) ready for action. You want to pick a sucker that has spear shaped leaves, they are the best ones to get babies going. You can also chop a piece of the root system of the mother plant but that may attract bugs and diseases. Blast the base of the banana tree and pull out the water until you can see where the baby is attaching to the mother. Use the chisel to then slice off the baby.

This also allows you to add fresh earth to the plant
